name: Jehoshaphat
title: Father of the prophet Micaiah
summary: Jehoshaphat is known from the Old Testament as the father of the prophet Micaiah, who prophesied during King Ahab's reign in Israel. He is mentioned primarily to identify his son, who was a true prophet speaking God's word even when it was unpopular. Jehoshaphat himself plays no independent role in the narratives but is important as the father of a courageous prophet.

keyEvents.title: Micaiah son of Jehoshaphat is summoned before the kings
keyEvents.description: King Ahab and King Jehoshaphat of Judah wanted to consult a true prophet before going to war against Ramoth in Gilead. Micaiah, son of Jehoshaphat, was brought forward as the only remaining prophet who spoke the truth.

keyEvents.title: Jehoshaphat identified through Ahab's reference
keyEvents.description: King Ahab referred to Micaiah, son of Jehoshaphat, and expressed his hatred for him because he never prophesied anything good about the king, but only evil.

keyEvents.title: Micaiah son of Jehoshaphat's prophecy concerning Ahab's defeat
keyEvents.description: Micaiah, son of Jehoshaphat, prophesied that Ahab would fall in battle at Ramoth in Gilead and described a vision from the Lord's throne room where a lying spirit was sent to Ahab's prophets.

keyEvents.title: The parallel account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The same account about Micaiah, son of Jehoshaphat, and his prophecy against Ahab is recounted in 2 Chronicles, where Jehoshaphat is again mentioned as the father's identifier.

keyEvents.title: Micaiah son of Imlah imprisoned for his prophecy
keyEvents.description: After speaking the truth, Micaiah son of Imlah was thrown into prison on King Ahab's orders, where he was to remain on bread and water until the king returned in peace—which never happened.
